key_insight: A machine learning-guided SCAPS-1D workflow identified an optimal CdSnP2-based solar-cell/photodetector stack that significantly boosts both power conversion and sensing performance.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that data-driven optimization of layer thickness, doping, defects, and band alignment can accelerate the design of multifunctional optoelectronic devices.
method: SCAPS-1D simulations generated training data for device variants
Six ML models plus one deep learning model were trained to predict performance
SHAP was used to explain which layers and interface band offsets most affected outcomes
evidence_signal: The optimized n-CdS/p-CdSnP2/p+-CGS design improved efficiency from 20.67% to 32.69%, responsivity from 0.53 to 0.72 A W−1, and detectivity from 2.51×10^14 to 1.78×10^16 Jones.
watch_item: The reported gains come from simulation-driven optimization, so experimental validation and fabrication tolerance checks are still needed before deployment.
paper_title: Machine learning-assisted design and explainable optimization of CdSnP2-based integrated solar-photodetector devices
